title: Uninformed and informed search
subtitle: Problem solving as finding a path through a space of states: blind search, then search that can see where the goal is.

formal.title: Formulating a problem
formal.body: A well-defined search problem has an initial state, a set of actions, a transition model (state + action → state), a goal test and a path cost. A route-finding problem: states are cities, actions are roads, cost is distance. A solution is a sequence of actions from start to goal; an optimal solution has least cost. Search strategies are compared on completeness, optimality, time and space.

unin.title: Breadth-first and depth-first
unin.body: BFS expands the shallowest node first (a FIFO queue): complete, optimal when steps cost the same, but memory grows as bᵈ. DFS expands the deepest first (a stack): tiny memory, but can dive forever and need not find the shortest path. Iterative deepening runs depth-limited DFS with limits 0, 1, 2… combining BFS’s optimality with DFS’s memory. On the small maze: BFS cost 5, DFS cost 5 (a longer, legal route).

heur.title: Heuristics: greedy best-first and A*
heur.body: A heuristic h(n) estimates the cost from n to the goal (here the Manhattan distance). Greedy best-first expands the node with the smallest h: fast, but not optimal. A* expands the smallest f(n) = g(n) + h(n), where g is the cost so far: it is optimal if h is admissible (never overestimates). On an open 4×8 grid BFS expands 32 cells, greedy 11 and A* 11 — all three find the cost-10 path except greedy may not in general.

csp.title: Constraint satisfaction
csp.body: A CSP has variables, domains and constraints (map colouring: neighbouring regions differ; sudoku; timetabling). Solve by backtracking: assign a variable, check constraints, undo on failure. Improve with constraint propagation (node/arc/path consistency) and variable-ordering heuristics (most constrained first).
csp.steps: Colour WA, NT, SA, Q with 3 colours so neighbours differ. SA touches WA, NT and Q, so colour it first (most constrained). SA = red; WA = green, NT = blue (differs from both), Q = green (differs from NT and SA).

cmp.title: Comparing strategies
cmp.steps: Branching factor b = 3, solution depth d = 4: BFS generates about 1 + 3 + 9 + 27 + 81 nodes.

summary.title: Summary
summary.body:
• BFS: shortest in steps; DFS: small memory; A*: optimal and focused with an admissible heuristic.
  • CSP: backtracking plus propagation.
